items.rationale: The frame sustained theft damage, so §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 allow a like-for-like replacement. The €250 gross estimate is reduced to €134.41 under the shared €500 mobility cap (§4.2.2).
The brakes sustained theft damage, so §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 allow equivalent replacements. The €139 gross estimate is reduced to €74.73 under the shared mobility cap.
The tracker helped locate the bike, but no theft damage to or separate loss of the tracker is established. Sections 4.2.3 and 7.1.8(b) exclude its replacement; the amount shown is hypothetical.
Sections 3.1.6 and 7.1.5 independently exclude routine servicing and work on the unaffected second bicycle. The amount shown is hypothetical.
Sections 4.2.3 and 7.1.8(b) exclude supplementary equipment not itself shown to have been stolen or damaged. The amount shown is hypothetical for both items.
Necessary shipping of replacement parts is covered under §7.1.7(f), but shipping for the new accessories is not. Assuming €25 gross is attributable to the covered repair, its capped share is €13.44.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(f) require evidence that this was a necessary repair attendance distinct from shipping or recovery transport. If substantiated at €25 gross, its share after including it in the capped pool would be about €13.09.

Fitting the replacement frame and brakes is covered by §7.1.7(c), excluding work on the second bike and any labour charged twice. Estimated distinct assembly of €140 gross is reduced to €75.27 under the shared cap.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers consumables used on the theft repair only, subject to allocation under §7.1.10. Estimated eligible sundries of €8 gross are reduced to €4.30 under the shared cap.

Section 7.1.7(d) covers separately stated apprentice time attributable to the theft repair, not servicing or labour already included in assembly. One eligible hour at €18 gross is reduced to €9.68 under the shared cap.
Sections 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.8(g) allow necessary skilled repair time not already charged as assembly. One eligible hour at €38 gross is reduced to €20.43 under the shared cap.
Section 5.2.2(a) expressly covers the necessary initial attendance to recover the bicycle. Estimated travel and attendance of €32 gross are reduced to €17.20 under the shared mobility cap.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers cutting and removing the lock to release the stolen bicycle. Estimated gross cost of €105 for the whole line is reduced to €56.45 under the shared mobility cap.

Sections 5.2.2(a) and 7.1.8(f) cover a second attendance only if recovery required it; the description does not establish that need. If substantiated at €32 gross, its share after including it in the capped pool would be about €16.63.

items.description: Mandatory impound release and storage fee
items.rationale: The yard's unavoidable release charge is covered under §5.2.2(c), not excluded as claims handling. The €100 fee plus 19% VAT gives €119 gross; applying the €500 cap to the estimated €930 eligible pool gives €63.98.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim-processing charges, unlike the yard's mandatory release fee. The amount shown is hypothetical.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers labour of every grade used to release the bicycle, provided it is not already included in the cutting charge. One eligible hour at €18 gross is reduced to €9.68 under the shared cap.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled labour needed to release the bicycle, with duplicate charges excluded under §7.1.8(g). One eligible hour at €38 gross is reduced to €20.43 under the shared cap.
